name: Personal Experience Markers
description: Examines the text for authentic linguistic markers of personal lived experience. While Large Language Models can simulate first-person narratives (e.g., 'When I was a child...'), these generations often lack the specific, granular sensory details, emotional continuity, and localized spatial/temporal references that human writers naturally embed when recalling genuine memories.
mechanism: The algorithm scans for a convergence of three feature sets: Episodic specificities (exact times, hyper-specific locations, anomalous physical details), Sensory lexicon (words correlating to smell, touch, specific colors, or localized sounds), and Emotional-temporal grounding (how feelings are anchored to specific events in the past). When instructed to write a personal story, LLMs tend to generate high-level, trope-heavy abstracts (e.g., 'The sun beat down on my face as I realized the value of hard work'). They overuse universal emotional cliches and drastically under-represent mundane but authentic granular details (e.g., 'The steering wheel was sticky from the spilled soda'). Furthermore, AI struggles to maintain emotional continuity across a long narrative without constantly reiterating the moral lesson. The system measures the density of these authentic 'episodic markers' against the presence of generic 'narrative tropes' to calculate an 'Authenticity Deficit Score'.
useCase: Crucial for verifying the authenticity of college admission essays, personal blog posts, cover letters, and product reviews where establishing genuine human experience is the primary goal.
strengths:
• Highly effective at detecting AI-generated 'sob stories', fake product reviews, and generic college application essays.
• Targets the fundamental inability of a statistical model to hallucinate complex, consistent, and mundane human memories.
limitations:
• Prone to false positives when a human writer is deliberately writing abstractly, philosophically, or writing a highly professional biography that omits sensory details.
• Advanced prompt engineering ('act as a human and include highly specific sensory details and mundane observations') can significantly reduce the effectiveness of this metric.
parameters:
Analysis: NER for Spatial/Temporal markers and Lexical analysis for Sensory/Emotional Grounding
Metric: Density of Episodic Specificity vs. Narrative Tropes
Output: 0-100 Authenticity Deficit (Simulated Experience) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 70-80% accuracy. Excellent at catching lazy, unprompted AI narratives, but can struggle against highly detailed, iteratively prompted synthetic stories.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Bandi, A. et al. (2023). Lexical Features of AI-Generated vs Human-Written Text. IEEE.
